name: state_mou_5yr_sweep
what: 5-year (2021-2026) state investor-summit MoU sweep, 12 states/state-pairs via parallel subagents. Distinct from layer 42 (revealed, verified investment EVENTS) and layer 16 (policy-eligible scheme data) -- this is the intermediate 'MoU signed' stage, with follow_through_status tracked per record since Indian state MoUs are well-documented to frequently not convert to real investment.

This is a partisan claim I could not independently verify company-by-company, but it is directionally consistent with how few of the aggregate-total companies in Davos press coverage turned out, on individual verification, to be foreign-headquartered.

I could not verify PRYM Aerospace's country of headquarters or confirm/refute the 'nonexistent factory' allegation from independent sources, so it is omitted from the verified list; flagged here as a specific, serious 'MoU graveyard'-style red flag worth follow-up.

I could not independently confirm company names, investment figures, or exact dates for these from a primary or clearly reliable secondary source within the available search budget (the main Business Standard Davos-2023 article returned an HTTP 403 and could not be read). Omitted from the verified list pending confirmation; noted here because if genuine, they would meet this dataset's criteria.

'Temasek Capital Management' (Singapore) is named in multiple Davos-2025 company lists but no source found gave a specific investment figure for it individually (only the aggregate MoU-total context). Omitted from the mous list for lack of a verifiable figure/detail, though its foreign status (Singapore) is not in doubt.

This is the single most concrete, sourced data point found on Maharashtra's actual Davos MoU conversion rate, and is offered as important context for interpreting the many 'no follow-up news found' statuses above — most of those reflect genuine immaturity (MoUs signed within the last 0-2 years) rather than confirmed abandonment.

Large aggregate/headline totals reported by the state government and press for each Davos trip (e.g., 'Rs 30 lakh crore signed at Davos 2026', 'Rs 15.70 lakh crore at Davos 2025', 'Rs 1.37 lakh crore at Davos 2023', 'US$184 billion at Magnetic Maharashtra') are self-reported at the moment of signing and were deliberately NOT used as data points in the mous[] list above — only individually named companies with a specific, sourced investment figure were included, consistent with this dataset's goal of avoiding uncritical repetition of summit press-release totals.

This sweep's WebSearch budget (200 queries, shared across the session) was exhausted partway through research on Davos 2026 (Bosch, CapitaLand-vs-Davos overlap, Coca-Cola, Iron Mountain, Fineman Global, JBL, Essar Renewables were identified by name in aggregate lists but could not be individually verified for country-of-headquarters/investment figure/date via a second corroborating source before the budget ran out). Web search quota was exhausted mid-sweep; remaining verification relied on WebFetch against already-identified URLs and Wikipedia, so several promising leads (Foxconn housing investment, Delta Electronics, Crocs, Evervan Kothari, ANSR) could not be independently confirmed and were left out or moved to negative_notes rather than reported as verified.
negative_notes: Aggregate summit totals were deliberately excluded as data points: GIM 2024 press claimed 631 MoUs worth Rs 6.64 lakh crore (~USD 80 billion, ~2.69 million jobs); a separate 'Investment Conclave' claimed 104 MoUs worth Rs 1.02 lakh crore; a July 2022 event claimed 60 MoUs worth Rs 1.25 lakh crore; a Coimbatore Investors' Conclave claimed 59 MoUs worth Rs 34,000 crore. These are the classic 'MoU graveyard' headline figures this sweep was designed to look past — only individually named, sourced foreign companies from within these totals were extracted into the mous list above.

Daimler India Commercial Vehicles (Germany, via Daimler Truck) — Rs 2,277 crore Oragadam plant-expansion MoU — found and well-sourced, but dated to May 2020, which falls outside the 2021-2026 window specified for this sweep. Excluded on date grounds only.

Salcomp PLC (Finland) — Rs 1,300 crore expansion of its Nokia Telecom SEZ facility in Sriperumbudur — sources gave conflicting dates (one ties it to the 2019 GIM, another to a May 2020 batch of 17 foreign-investor MoUs). Could not pin down a date inside the 2021-2026 window with confidence, so excluded.

The 'Tamil Nadu signs MoUs with 17 foreign investors' batch (Rs 15,218 crore, companies from France, Taiwan, Japan, China, including IGL Transplantation Solutions and Vivid Solaire Energy) is dated May 2020 — just before this sweep's window — and was excluded on date grounds, not for lack of verifiability.

Feng Tay Group (Taiwan) — operates a large existing footwear manufacturing presence in Tamil Nadu (Lotus, East Wind, Fairway units in Cheyyar/Bargur, reportedly ~40,000 workers) — but the only dated MoU/announcement material found in this sweep is from 2006 (original MoU) and a 2020 announcement of two more factories, both outside the 2021-2026 window. A fresh Feng Tay MoU within the window may exist but was not found/verified here.

Foxconn / Hon Hai — a ~Rs 706 crore worker-housing/residential-complex investment was referenced in a secondary source (via a synthesized theprint.in summary) as occurring around August 2024, but the original article could not be located and read directly, so neither the exact date nor whether it constitutes a formal state MoU (versus a company-internal capex decision) could be confirmed. Excluded pending direct-source verification. Foxconn's large pre-existing Sriperumbudur mobile-assembly campus is real and operational but its founding MoU predates this window.

Delta Electronics (Taiwan) — referenced in the same secondary source as employing ~20,000 in Tamil Nadu electronics manufacturing, but no MoU date or investment figure was found; excluded pending verification.

Crocs — appeared only as a Deccan Herald headline ('Crocs footwear to be manufactured in Tamil Nadu') found via search snippet; the article body was never opened due to WebSearch quota exhaustion, so company nationality confirmation, investment figure, sector detail, and date are all unverified. Excluded.

Evervan Kothari — referenced in a Deccan Herald headline (Rs 5,000 crore non-leather footwear units in Karur/Perambalur) found only via snippet; the 'Kothari' component of the name suggests a joint venture with an Indian partner, and foreign-HQ status could not be confirmed. Excluded.

ANSR — signed a GCC (Global Capability Centre) facilitation MoU with Guidance Tamil Nadu in November 2025, but ANSR's headquarters appears to be dual US (Austin, Texas)/India (Bengaluru), and this sweep could not clearly establish it as a foreign-headquartered company for this dataset's purposes. Excluded pending verification.

The Vettri Tamil Nadu Investors' Conclave (2026-08-13) source also reported 'seven institutional MoUs...with companies and organisations from Kazakhstan, New Zealand and Russia' without naming the specific entities. Excluded because no individual company names were available in the source read.

Singapore Investment Conclave (2023-05-25) also produced MoUs with Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and Singapore-India Partnership Office (multiple, with SIPCOT/FaMe TN/TANSIM) — these are institutional/academic/government-to-government cooperation MoUs, not individually named foreign company investments, so they were excluded from the mous list even though they are genuine and dated.

WebSearch quota (200 calls/session) was exhausted partway through this sweep. Remaining research relied on WebFetch against already-known URLs, Wikipedia, and Bing search-result pages (which returned only generic listings, not usable detail). This means several plausible additional TN foreign-MoU candidates from 2021-2026 almost certainly exist but were not found in this pass — this list should be treated as a verified subset, not an exhaustive one.

negative_notes: Minda Corporation (Spark Minda / Uno Minda group) appears prominently in both the Feb-2026 Japan-visit coverage and the Aug-2026 UP-Japan Investment Meet (Rs 1,166 crore, YEIDA Sectors 10 & 24) but is headquartered in India (New Delhi/Noida) and was excluded per this sweep's foreign-only scope, despite being marketed alongside genuinely Japanese signatories.

Fuji Silvertech / Fujisilvertech Concrete Pvt Ltd was named in one secondary source (an X/Twitter post attributed to 'The Uttar Pradesh Index') as part of the Feb-2026 Japan-visit MoU batch, but could not be corroborated in any article this sweep fetched, and its sector/HQ could not be independently verified. Left out rather than guessed.

BAE Systems (UK) was reported as having met UP delegation officials ('preparing for big investment') around UPGIS-2023, but no source found describes an actual signed MoU — this looks like an exploratory meeting, not a verified MoU, so it was excluded.

UK partner-country session at UPGIS-2023 reportedly produced '6 MoUs in security, technology and defence sectors,' and the UK announced defence/aerospace/medical investment intent generally, but no individually-named UK company signatory could be found in accessible coverage.

Singapore's partner-country session reportedly produced 6 new MoUs (urban infrastructure, waste management, IT parks, data centres, education) plus a separate ~Rs 29,000 crore 'spiritual and eco-tourism' investment pledge from unnamed 'investors from Singapore.' Only SLG Capital could be individually verified; the rest are unnamed in the press coverage this sweep found.

Star Consortium Private Limited was named alongside SLG Capital as signing a ~Rs 2,000 crore data-centre/logistics MoU with UPSIDA, but this sweep could not confirm whether it is foreign- or India-headquartered, so it was left out rather than assumed foreign.

Denmark-UP 'Smart Laboratory on Clean Rivers' (SLCR), signed as a ~Rs 1,000 crore MoU at UPGIS-2023 and formally launched in 2024 by NMCG/IIT-BHU/Government of Denmark, is a genuine, well-documented, and (unusually for this dataset) confirmed-active bilateral partnership — but it is a government-to-government MoU, not an individually-named foreign company, so it was excluded from the mous array per this state's task scope.

A May-2023 MoU between the UP government and Gyeongsangbuk-do province (South Korea) was found (invest.up.gov.in press release), but this is again a sub-national government partner, not a company, and was excluded on the same basis.

This sweep's central hypothesis going in — that UP's Ground Breaking Ceremony 3.0/4.0 events would give unusually good, checkable individual-company conversion data for UPGIS-2023 MoUs — did NOT pan out from publicly accessible coverage. GBC coverage found (organiser.org, thestatesman, businesstoday-style recaps) reports only aggregate figures (e.g., '1,406 projects worth Rs 80,000 crore' for GBC 3.0; '14,000 projects worth ~Rs 10 lakh crore' for GBC 4.0) and, where individual companies are named at all, they are overwhelmingly domestic real-estate/industrial names (Godrej Properties, Mahagun Infratech, Theme County, Roseberry Estate) rather than the internationally-branded UPGIS-2023 MoU signatories tracked in this file. No source found cross-references a specific foreign UPGIS-2023 signatory (e.g. IKEA, Lulu Group, HMI Group, SLG Capital) against a specific GBC groundbreaking event, so none of the 'no follow-up news found' verdicts above should be read as 'confirmed stalled' — they reflect a genuine absence of public foreign-company-level conversion tracking, not a documented failure to convert.

A January-2026 WEF Davos delegation reportedly secured UP investment-proposal MoUs worth 'nearly Rs 3 lakh crore,' and a separately-headlined figure of 'Rs 90,000 crore with various Japanese companies' also surfaced in search results — neither was chased down to individually-named foreign companies in this sweep due to running out of WebSearch budget partway through; both are flagged here as open leads for a follow-up sweep.

The exact calendar date of Ground Breaking Ceremony @3.0 could not be pinned down independently in this sweep (multiple candidate source pages returned HTTP 403); it is placed provisionally in the Aug/mid-2023 window based on its being reported as the ceremony preceding GBC @4.0 (Feb 2024).

sweep_files_meta.method: WebSearch + WebFetch across official BGBS site (bengalglobalsummit.com), WBIDC, Indian and international business press (Business Standard, Deccan Herald, Economic Times-linked wires, PTI/Wire syndications, sector trade press e.g. DataCenterDynamics/w.media for data centres, se.com/company press releases), Wikipedia (Bengal Silicon Valley Tech Hub, List of data centres in West Bengal, Economy of West Bengal) as a company-name index to then verify independently, and direct fetch of individual company press releases where reachable. IMPORTANT FINDING: coverage of BGBS 2022/2023/2025 is overwhelmingly aggregate (total MoU counts: 86 in 2019, 137 in 2022, 188 in 2023, 212 in 2025; total proposed investment in lakh-crore figures) and dominated by named INDIAN conglomerates (Reliance, ITC, JSW, Adani, RP-Sanjiv Goenka, Ambuja Neotia, Birla, TCG/Chatterjee Group, Emami). Individually-named FOREIGN company MoUs are rarely disclosed in press coverage of the summits themselves - most verified foreign-company entries below were found instead via sector/trade press (data centres, semiconductors, industrial capex press releases) covering real government-facilitated land/investment agreements in the same 2021-2026 window, rather than from a BGBS ceremony MoU list, and this distinction is flagged per-entry below. No official BGBS MoU signatory list or PDF naming individual companies was found publicly.
negative_notes: Aggregate BGBS totals by year (context only, not attributable to named foreign companies): 2019 - 86 MoUs, ~Rs 2.84 lakh crore proposed (outside the 2021-2026 window, included for trend context only); 2022 - 137 MoUs/LoIs/EoIs, ~Rs 3.42-3.76 lakh crore depending on source; 2023 - 188 MoUs, Rs 3,76,288 crore; 2025 - 212 MoUs/LoIs, Rs 4.40 lakh crore (some wire coverage cites Rs 91,000 crore as a narrower 'firm commitments' figure). None of the sources reviewed published a full itemised MoU signatory list.

BGBS 2022 partner-country delegations (Japan, Italy, Netherlands, UK, South Korea, US, Australia, New Zealand, Vietnam, Finland, Morocco, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Kenya) were reported as making country-level statements of interest (e.g. 'Japan and Italy want to invest in MSME sector') with NO individual company named or investment figure attached - excluded per task rules against uncritically repeating unverified summit rhetoric.

BGBS 2023 partner countries included Australia, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Fiji, France, Germany, Japan, Kenya, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Nepal, Netherlands, Poland, Rwanda, Slovak Republic, South Korea, and UK (17 countries, ~400 international delegates) - no company-level MoU breakdown by nationality was found in press coverage reviewed.

Mitsubishi Chemical Group - held exploratory talks with West Bengal government (Durgapur/Panagarh sites) re: a possible semiconductor supply-chain investment; as of the most recent reporting found (mid-2026), this remains preliminary discussion with NO MoU signed, no investment figure, and no timeline disclosed. Excluded from the verified list per instructions not to include unconfirmed proposals.

The Bengal government signed an MoU with Spain's La Liga (football league) to set up a football academy during one of CM Mamata Banerjee's overseas trips - this is a sports/cultural partnership, not a commercial investment/JV, so excluded as out of scope.

CM Mamata Banerjee's overseas roadshows (UK, Singapore in 2023; Italy/Germany in 2023 - visited Munich among other German cities with a business delegation, hosted by BVMW and the German Chambers of Commerce (IHK); Spain, Dubai/UAE legs also reported) were described in press as securing unspecified 'major MoUs' - no individually named foreign companies or investment figures were found for these legs despite targeted searching, so none are included.

Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd (HPL) - The Chatterjee Group (TCG), HPL's largest private shareholder, is US-based (Purnendu Chatterjee), but TCG/HPL's relationship with West Bengal dates to the 1980s-90s (pre-window) and its 'foreign' character is ambiguous (Indian-origin founder, long-standing joint promoter with the West Bengal government itself). A ~Rs 8,500 crore polycarbonate plant was reported as being 'explored' by HPL in March 2025, but no signed MoU or firm date was found. Excluded as ambiguous/unconfirmed.

Ricoh India (Japan-origin) appears in a West Bengal data-centre list (SALTLEC facility, marked operational) but this facility appears to predate the 2021-2026 window and no new MoU or investment event within the window was found for it - excluded.

Extensive searches for other plausible foreign investors in West Bengal in this window (Siemens, Bosch, ABB, DP World, Maersk/APM Terminals, PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Cargill, Kansai Nerolac, Asian Paints/Jotun, Suzuki, Toyota, Samsung, LG, DBS/HSBC/Standard Chartered/Citibank, Capgemini/Cognizant/Tech Mahindra land parcels in Bengal Silicon Valley) turned up either no West Bengal-specific investment news in this window, or land/office allocations without a confirmed investment figure or signing date precise enough to verify individually - none met the bar for inclusion.

No official, itemised, government-published MoU signatory list for any BGBS edition (2022, 2023, or 2025) could be located publicly - WBIDC's own summit page and the bengalglobalsummit.com overview pages describe the event format but do not name signatories. This opacity is itself consistent with the 'MoU graveyard' phenomenon the task describes: verifiable, individually-named foreign-company commitments are the exception in public reporting, not the rule.
